Omkar winked back and both grinned; it was clearly their private joke about Omkar always overshooting. A few minutes later, Sumit winked at Prachi when she asked to borrow his clamp. Prachi's face tightened; she took the clamp without a word and moved to the far bench. I don't think Sumit meant anything by it, but Prachi had no way of knowing that. After class I spoke to Sumit on his own. He looked surprised and said it was "just a thanks". I explained that a wink only works when the other person is in on the joke. He agreed to talk to Prachi, and before the end of the day I checked with her: he had apologised, and she said she was fine.

qa.a: It turned bright pink too early.

qa.a: Speaking to Sumit privately, explaining when a wink works, and checking with Prachi the same day, so her discomfort was taken seriously.

qa.a: To Sumit it was 'just a thanks', like the friendly wink with Omkar, so he didn't expect it to land differently with Prachi.
